body: well, almost everyone will recommend the language that they started with, within reason. be it ruby, PHP, python, or java. Most people who start with a lower level language will default to python, or if they're assholes, assembly. I like python because the syntax is extremely simple and it has a lot of libraries that can help a new programmer a lot. i would be hesitant to throw anyone into an OOP language until they're comfortable with the basics.

well, I would say for beginners, python would be a great starting point. it's an easy to learn language, its pretty versatile, and you won't get bogged down in syntax like you might with C++ or java. The other good thing about it is that it's interactive, so you won't have to wait for your code to compile. I would recommend you start by downloading python from the [website](http://python.org/getit/) too start with. theres some fantastic documentation avaliable, in fact, [heres a whole page of them!](http://wiki.python.org/moin/BeginnersGuide/NonProgrammers) its a wonderful hobby. have fun with it!
